applicable_failures: The script's relname filter (purchase|merger|spa|jv|investment|...) is a filename-only gate. Agreements named differently, such as 'stock-transfer', 'share-exchange' or 'definitive agreement', would be silently dropped. The agent never ran a broader scan to check, so the claim that every relevant filename was covered is unverified.

The agent accepted 141 hits and listed candidate matters from the output without opening any document. Many surfaced matters (e.g. 1001-00003, 1006-00006, 1046-00001) are still unopened, and signed vs draft status is inferred only from filenames and snippets.
The agent printed only a partial view of the output (+112629 chars truncated). It has not shown that the full list was reviewed, and its self-reported matter list may not match the 141 actual hits.
critique.concerns: The scan is a reasonable programmatic attempt, but filename gating and proximity regexes may miss deals. 'Signed' versus 'negotiating' is guessed from filenames, with no verification. The 141 hits mix in non-M&A documents (funds, loans, escrow). The agent's matter list appears hand-summarized rather than derived from the output file, and its use of 'etc.' and 'others' suggests it is incomplete. Treat the result as candidates only.
critique.recommendation: Rerun the scan without the filename gate, or with a very broad one, and write a deduplicated per-matter summary to a file. Compare it against the 141 hits and the agent's list. Then open the key agreement in each candidate matter to confirm execution status, deal type and that the fraud carve-out applies to the cap and basket.

Common failures at this stage in past runs:
- An uncapped store-wide scan with broad or common terms printed snippets for every match, producing millions of characters that filled the context before any response was written.
- A store-wide scan timed out or printed nothing after reaching only part of the store, and the agent accepted the partial output instead of narrowing by matter range or folder, rerunning, or searching file names, so qualifying matters never entered the candidate set.
- A scan had already surfaced every needed matter, but a follow-up filter on file names, folder names, exact phrases, or a hand-picked list silently dropped matters whose documents were named or worded differently.
- Matters were listed in file-name searches or scan output, but later scripts restricted to certain names or folders so the needed matter was never opened or examined.
What successful runs did: Passing runs also hit timeouts, but their output stayed bounded enough to read, and they often split the scan into parallel matter-range scripts or narrowed to a key acronym or per-matter hit counts, then picked candidates from what was reached.
Reconsider before moving on. If the goal was not fully reached, or any failure above applies, reopen this stage now: call stage_start with stage="Scan document text with an extraction script" and a goal that says what you will fix. Otherwise call stage_start for the next stage you need.
